race_name: UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya

top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before November.

Road-specific control matters at UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 65 miles.
UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya's mixed terrain rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya. Train it until it feels boring.
65 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
2-minute all-out efforts on mixed terrain. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what UCI Gran Fondo World Series Antalya's mixed terrain actually does to you.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
